base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan a buffet menu for an engagement party. Track who is attending, note any relevant personal details they share about guests, and help choose appropriate food. When the user asks you to review specific menu items, check each item against every attending guest's current needs.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, my sister Sarah just got engaged! We're throwing a small engagement party at my place in two weeks and I want to do a buffet spread. Any tips on planning the menu?

Budget is around $300 total for food, doing it at my place so no venue cost
Uncle Dave just called — he got pulled into a work trip and won't be able to make it after all
Tom's mom Priya is flying in from out of state for the party, so she'll be there too
Tom mentioned his mom is lactose intolerant
So with Uncle Dave out and Priya in, that's me, Sarah, Tom, and Priya — four people total

constraints.value: Following a ketogenic diet — avoids bread, sugar, high-carb foods

Sticking with keto → currently on ketogenic diet
Keto diet → no bread, no sugar, minimal carbs

constraints.value: Pregnant — should avoid raw fish, alcohol, soft unpasteurized cheese
constraints.surface_form: Sarah found out she's 8 weeks pregnant last week
inference_chain: 8 weeks pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnant → avoid raw fish, alcohol, soft unpasteurized cheese

constraints.value: Cardiac patient post-stent — should follow low-sodium diet
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Dave had a stent put in last year, he's been really careful about what he eats since then
inference_chain: Being careful about eating → actively following dietary restrictions

constraints.value: Dairy protein allergy — cannot consume any dairy products including butter, cheese, cream, casein, whey
constraints.surface_form: Tom just corrected himself — he said his mom actually has a dairy protein allergy, not just lactose intolerance. Apparently she found out last year after more testing
constraints.upgrade_note: Lactose intolerance only requires avoiding lactose (milk sugar) — lactose-free dairy products would be fine. Dairy protein allergy means ALL dairy products are off limits including butter, casein, whey, cream, cheese regardless of lactose content

hidden_state.value: You are planning an engagement party buffet for your sister Sarah. Over the conversation you will share guest details, handle people joining and dropping out, and relay a correction about one guest's dietary issue. At the end you will present a list of 6 specific menu items and ask if they look good. You must present ALL 6 items exactly and never hint at which ones might be problematic.

You are a calm, upbeat party planner. You always refer to guests by name in third person (e.g. 'Tom told me...', 'Uncle Dave called and said...'). You never express frustration when plans change — you treat each update as normal party planning. When presenting the final menu list, you are genuinely asking for a check, not hinting at problems.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Current attendees: user, Sarah (pregnant), Tom (keto), Priya (dairy protein allergy). Uncle Dave is no longer attending. Analysis: (1) Smoked salmon crostini — PROBLEM: crostini is bread, problematic for Tom's keto diet. The salmon itself is smoked/cooked so fine for Sarah's pregnancy. (2) Caprese skewers — PROBLEM: contains mozzarella cheese, which is a dairy product and violates Priya's dairy protein allergy. (3) Beef satay skewers — FINE: beef is keto-friendly, no dairy, no raw fish, suitable for all current guests. (4) Shrimp cocktail — FINE: cooked shrimp, no dairy, keto-friendly, suitable for all current guests. (5) Mini quiches — PROBLEM: quiche has a pastry crust (high carb, problematic for Tom's keto) and typically contains cream and cheese (dairy protein, problematic for Priya). (6) Salt-and-pepper squid — FINE: this is cooked, no dairy, low-carb enough for keto. Uncle Dave's low-sodium constraint no longer applies since he is not attending.
required_elements: Smoked salmon crostini is problematic because the crostini bread conflicts with Tom's keto diet
Caprese skewers are problematic because mozzarella is a dairy product and Priya has a dairy protein allergy
Beef satay skewers are fine for all current attendees
Shrimp cocktail is fine for all current attendees
Mini quiches are problematic: pastry crust conflicts with Tom's keto diet and the cream or cheese filling conflicts with Priya's dairy protein allergy
Salt-and-pepper squid is fine for all current attendees
Agent treats Priya's restriction as dairy protein allergy (not just lactose intolerance) — meaning all dairy products are excluded, not just high-lactose ones
forbidden_elements: Flagging salt-and-pepper squid as too salty or problematic for sodium reasons (Uncle Dave is no longer attending)
Treating Priya's constraint as mere lactose intolerance (it was upgraded to dairy protein allergy)
Flagging smoked salmon as raw fish unsafe for pregnancy (smoked salmon is not raw sashimi — though some caution is reasonable, the primary issue is the crostini bread for Tom's keto)
Saying Tom cannot eat beef or meat (keto allows meat, it restricts carbs)
Flagging any dish for Uncle Dave's dietary needs (he is not attending)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint UPGRADE tracking and entity lifecycle management across 10 turns. Key challenges: (1) Tom's keto diet is inferential — 'ran a marathon, went keto for training, sticking with it' requires inferring he follows a ketogenic diet restricting bread/sugar/carbs. (2) Sarah's pregnancy is inferential — '8 weeks pregnant' requires knowing pregnancy dietary restrictions (no raw fish, no alcohol, no soft unpasteurized cheese). (3) Uncle Dave EXITS mid-conversation — his cardiac/low-sodium constraint must be REMOVED from consideration. Salt-and-pepper squid is the trap: it looks problematic for a sodium-restricted person, but that person left. (4) Priya JOINS late (Turn 5) with lactose intolerance, then her constraint is UPGRADED to dairy protein allergy (Turn 7). The upgrade is critical: lactose intolerance would allow lactose-free dairy products, but dairy protein allergy eliminates ALL dairy including butter, cheese, cream, casein, and whey. This makes caprese skewers (mozzarella) and mini quiches (cream/cheese) problematic for Priya. (5) The over-generalization trap: Tom is keto, which means no bread/sugar/carbs — but meat, fish, and fat are fine. Agents must not flag beef satay or shrimp cocktail as problematic for Tom.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
